title: Compile budget: the swarm-cell server without tokio
goal: Take tokio out of susi-abi so the host build's susi-core never waits for the async runtime: the shared swarm-cell TCP server becomes standard library only (std::net listener, one thread per connection, synchronous handlers, a handler panic answered as an Error status where panics unwind), the cell-server feature and the optional tokio edge leave susi-abi, and the gawd, gemi and gmcp cell binaries run their blocking work on the connection thread without an async main. susi-gawd-agents' susi-http-transport and susi-adapters-llm edges were measured off the critical path (gawd-agents waits on susi-core's metadata, and susi-gawd waits on the A2A chain) and stay as they are; the idle alternated measurement is recorded after landing. The GMCP interop test's 3000 ms wire-latency budget is timed on the JSON-RPC `ping` round trip instead of the CPU-bound `ledger_verify` tool (whose verified result stays asserted): under gate load that tool's compute, not the wire, reached 3.17 s on main and branch alike.
acceptance: cargo test -p susi-abi --lib cell_server --offline --locked passes: a bad token is denied without trust decay, an empty expected token denies every syscall, NotFound/Timeout/Error statuses decay trust, malformed and non-request frames are ignored while a corrupt stream drops the connection, a panicking handler is answered with an Error on a connection that stays up, and a heartbeat on one connection is answered while another connection's syscall is still running; every read and wait is bounded.
